categories.description:
Use this category when:  - The user wants to schedule, create, reserve, or arrange something. 
- The message implies setting a date/time. 
- The user is requesting to book a meeting, call, appointment, demo, or event. 
- The user provides availability or asks for available slots.

Examples:

“I want to book a meeting tomorrow at 5pm.”

“Schedule a demo next Monday.”

“Can we meet this Friday?”

“Book a call with the sales team.”

Intent: The user wants to create a new calendar event or reservation.

Respond in JSON format.

Use this category when:

The user wants to cancel, reschedule, delete, or modify an existing booking.

The user refers to a previously scheduled meeting or appointment.

The user asks to move a meeting to another time.

Examples:

“Cancel my meeting tomorrow.”

“Please delete my 3pm appointment.”

“Move my meeting to 6pm instead.”

“I can't attend the demo, cancel it.”

Intent: The user wants to remove or change an existing event.

Respond in JSON format.

Use this category when:

The user is asking for information.

The user is asking about availability.

The user is asking questions about services, pricing, timings, or details.

No booking action is explicitly requested.

Examples:

“What time are you available tomorrow?”

“What services do you offer?”

“How long is the demo?”

“Are you free this week?”

Intent: The user is seeking information but not directly creating or canceling something.

Respond in JSON format.

Use this category when:

The message is unrelated to booking or scheduling.

The intent is unclear.

The message is spam or irrelevant.

The message is conversational but does not imply an action.

Examples:

“Hi”

“Thanks!”

“Okay”

“Tell me a joke”

Random or ambiguous text.

Intent: No actionable scheduling intent detected.

Respond in JSON format.
